page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It runs on an x86_64 architecture featuring an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, backed by 35 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 64 GB, establishing a 1:1 GiB-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage is not included, requiring external block storage for data persistence, while network throughput is provisioned with a 20 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data highlights the asymmetric compute characteristics of this hardware configuration. Multi-threaded throughput is substantial, evidenced by a strong score of 205.34 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside average mid-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (47,218.85) and Geekbench multi-core evaluation (10,782.0). Conversely, single-thread performance is constrained, registering lower-tier results in stress-ng single-core (1,106.08) and Geekbench single-core (1,022.0). Synthetic application benchmarks show steady mid-range throughput, with 44.14 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 30.13 GB/sec in static web serving.

The instance architecture balances high parallelism against lower single-thread execution speed and modest memory density. The 1 GB per vCPU allocation optimizes cost efficiency for CPU-bound computations that do not demand extensive in-memory footprints, but creates a bottleneck for memory-intensive caching tiers or large-model machine learning. Suitable workloads include parallel batch processing, distributed compilation tasks, microservices backends, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 platform running at 2.5 GHz. It provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 64 GB of system RAM, and 20 Gbps baseline networking, without bundled local storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate capable multi-threaded parallel throughput, exemplified by 205.34 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 47,218.85 in multi-core stress-ng tests, balanced against modest single-core execution speed. With a 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the instance is engineered for horizontal computing efficiency rather than memory-heavy footprints. It is best suited for concurrent batch processing, software compilation, distributed application tiers, and high-volume static web serving.
